recipes.name: CAJUN FOOD
ingredients: 8 ounces beer (just not a light beer!)
1 lb andouille sausage, cut into coins (or smoked kielbasa)
2 cups red wine (full bodied like Malbec or Cabernet Sauvignon)
1 pound andouille sausage, sliced into coins
instructions: For Chicken & Sausage Gumbo:

Take green bell pepper, celery, and white onion (also known as the “holy trinity”) and dice them into medium-sized pieces. Set aside for later. - 1 small green bell pepper diced - 2 ribs celery diced - 1 small white onion diced
Mince garlic cloves and set aside for later. - 6 garlic cloves minced

To make the roux, add vegetable oil to a pot and allow it to get smoking hot before adding all purpose flour. Using a wooden spoon or preferably a whisk, mix together until the consistency is similar to wet sand. - ½ cup vegetable oil - ½ cup all purpose flour

Within 30 seconds, the roux should be the color of milk chocolate. The darker the roux gets, the more you need to stir it, but let it sit for a few seconds before continuing to stir. After about 5-6 minutes, the color of the roux should be nice and dark or similar to the color of a Hershey’s chocolate bar. Set aside some of the roux to use later.
Add bay leaves as well as your “holy trinity” to the pot. Make sure to set aside some of the holy trinity mix for later. - 2 bay leaves - For the holy trinity
Once the mixture calms down a bit, add the minced garlic to the pot. Let the roux sit for 30 seconds. - 6 garlic cloves minced

Add beer and stir it in and whisk to prevent the mixture from becoming clumpy. Then, add chicken stock and whisk using the same procedure as the beer. - 8 ounces beer (just not a light beer!) - 4 cups chicken stock
Take andouille sausage or smoked kielbasa and cut into coins. - 1 lb andouille sausage cut into coins (or smoked kielbasa)

Add kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to both sides of boneless, skinless chicken thighs. Sear the chicken thighs in a smoking hot pan with oil. - kosher salt - 1 lb boneless skinless, chicken thighs
Add cayenne pepper and a pinch of salt to the roux. - 1 tbsp cayenne pepper - kosher salt

Turn the stovetop temperature to the lowest simmer possible and add a generous amount of black pepper to the roux. Then, add smoked paprika and stir. - freshly ground black pepper - 1 tbsp smoked paprika

After browning the chicken, add it straight to the pot and set aside the remaining oil from the chicken. Next, add the chopped up sausage or smoked kielbasa to the pot. - 1 lb boneless skinless, chicken thighs - 1 lb andouille sausage cut into coins (or smoked kielbasa)
Bring the roux to a bare simmer, cover it, and let sit for a couple of hours.
Serve with cooked white rice, garnish with scallions, and enjoy! - cooked white rice for serving - sliced scallions for garnish
For Rillions:
Remove all of the skin from the pork belly and add the skin to the roux. - 2 lbs pork belly skin removed - roux (from gumbo)

Take the fat from the pork belly and cut into chunks. Add the pork belly to a baking pan and season it with a few pinches of salt. Lightly mix to let the salt soak in. Set it aside and start preparing the red wine caramel. - 2 lbs pork belly skin removed - kosher salt
Add sugar and red wine to a pot. Bring to a rolling boil and whisk to create a syrup-like consistency. - 2 cups sugar - 2 cups red wine (full bodied like Malbec or Cabernet Sauvignon)
Sprinkle fresh thyme onto the pork belly. - fresh thyme - 2 lbs pork belly skin removed

Take the pot of red wine caramel and pour it straight on top of the pork belly. Make sure that the mixture is compact before placing it into a 400 degree Fahrenheit oven for 25-35 minutes and toss occasionally. Let cool for 10-15 minutes and serve with a slotted spoon. - 2 lbs pork belly skin removed - 2 cups red wine (full bodied like Malbec or Cabernet Sauvignon) - 2 cups sugar
For Dirty Rice:
For the Roux

To make the roux, add vegetable oil to a Dutch oven or pot and allow it to get smoking hot before adding all purpose flour. Using a wooden spoon or preferably a whisk, mix together until the consistency is similar to wet sand. - 1 tbsp vegetable oil - ¼ cup vegetable oil - ¼ cup all purpose flour

Within 30 seconds, the roux should be the color of milk chocolate. The darker the roux gets, the more you need to stir it, but let it sit for a few seconds before continuing to stir. After about 5-6 minutes, the color of the roux should be nice and dark or similar to the color of a Hershey’s chocolate bar. - For the Roux
For the ‘holy trinity’
Mince green pepper, celery, and onion into small pieces. - 1 small green bell pepper diced - 2 ribs celery diced - 1 small white onion diced
For the Dirty Rice
Press the ground beef into one large patty. - 1 lb ground beef
Add a generous amount of fresh black pepper and salt as well as cumin and cayenne (to taste) ground beef. - kosher salt - fresh black pepper - cumin to taste - cayenne to taste
Place the meat into a pan with hot vegetable oil. Once both sides are seared, roughly break it into pieces. - 1 lb ground beef

Add ‘holy trinity’ and crushed garlic to the pan. After the vegetables finish cooking, add roux and let it warm up for a minute before adding beer and chicken stock to the pan. Let simmer for about 45 minutes or until the consistency is a bit thicker. - For the holy trinity - 4 cloves garlic crushed - For the Roux - ⅓ cup beer (not a light one!) - 2 cups chicken stock
Add cooked white rice, a few pinches of salt, garnish with scallions, and enjoy! - 3 cups cooked white rice - scallions for garnish
For Jambalaya:

Reheat the leftover dirty rice and add andouille sausage (sliced into coins) as well as boneless chicken thighs (whole or cut up). - dirty rice (see ingredients above) - 1 pound andouille sausage sliced into coins - 4 boneless chicken thighs
Garnish with scallions and enjoy! - scallions for garnish
